statement: Source implementations disagree about DualSense LED brightness encoding: nowrep/dualsensectl accepts 0, 1 and 2 and sets valid_flag2 bit 0 with the brightness byte, and XInput_HID labels 0/1/2 bright/mid/dim; yesbotics protocol notes instead list 1/2/3 full/medium/low and describe a different flag interaction. The common brightness field is source-backed, but the exact retail encoding, which physical LEDs are affected, and revision-dependent behavior are not resolved. This is a source conflict, not a physically observed contradiction.

applicability.revision: pinned source implementations nowrep d3ae2fa, XInput_HID 11cf2ea, yesbotics 24203b8; retail firmware and hardware revision not measured
applicability.scope: DualSense output common byte 42 and valid_flag2 bit 0 (common byte 38). Compare nowrep main.c 591-608, XInput_HID dualsense.cpp 23-43 and 162-175, and yesbotics README_PROTOCOL.md 310-327. Previous ds-l0-led-led-brightness-levels was unknown; evidence now identifies conflicting interpretations, not a proven physical setting.
